idiom_name: Django template.Library filters/simple_tag, Jinja2 Environment.filters and globals
implementation_notes: Helpers are functions registered into a template registry: Django's custom tags and filters live in a templatetags module of an installed app behind a template.Library instance (@register.filter, @register.simple_tag, plus is_safe/needs_autoescape flags) and are loaded with {% load %}; Jinja2 registers them per Environment in env.filters / env.tests / env.globals. The classic helper object collapses into a function - only the responsibility split must not collapse: filters format and adapt, while retrieval stays in the view/queryset that fills the context. Express rendering intent with the engine's safe API (format_html, mark_safe, Markup) instead of returning strings concatenated from data. The classic helper class is only worth its weight when several filters share configuration (a formatter table or locale set), which is rare in practice.
pitfalls: A filter that introduces markup must be marked safe (format_html, mark_safe, is_safe=True) or autoescaping will escape the tags; marking it safe without escaping the interpolated data is the injection path.
Django's template language has no exception handling, so an exception raised in a filter becomes a server error - return a fallback value for malformed input.
templatetags modules are discovered at load time: a new module needs its app in INSTALLED_APPS and a server restart, otherwise the tag silently does not exist and the template errors at render.
Jinja2 environments must not gain filters after the first template is loaded; configure one Environment per app at start-up instead of registering lazily.
